current_activity: four tanks sent to counterattack meet US Task Force Mills at Büsbach, Stolberg, and fall back
notes: Event date: 15 September 1944, midmorning (MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 4). Event definition: By midmorning of 15 September the armour of Task Force Mills (3rd Armored Division) runs into four tanks of the brigade and four assault guns of the 9th Panzer Division at Büsbach, a suburb of Stolberg, sent to counterattack Task Force Lovelady; the German tanks fall back (MacDonald, ch. 4); Wikipedia has the brigade defending the West Wall at Stolberg from 15 to 23 September. Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 4, p. 76: "the armor ran abruptly into four tanks of the 105th Panzer Brigade and four organic assault guns of the 9th Panzer Division"; Wikipedia, List of German brigades in World War II: "Defended Westwall fortifications at Stolberg between 15 and 23 September". Location: Büsbach, Stolberg, North Rhine-Westphalia (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: MacDonald names Buesbach; Wikipedia names Stolberg. Opponents: US 3rd Armored Division (Task Forces Mills and Lovelady, Combat Command B).
